summary: Morgan, a narrator who suspects a setup, takes a phone call from Alan saying their trip must leave today despite the storm. Morgan believes Alan is lying and is being used to get Morgan out of town, which confirms the narrator is on Sarah's trail. Alan refuses to explain, rushes Morgan, and forbids a phone call to Steve, demanding Morgan be out front in nineteen minutes. The excerpt is part 118 of Book 3 of a fiction work.
one_line: Morgan suspects a setup when Alan suddenly insists they leave for the mountains today despite the storm, and is rushed out without making a call.
key_facts: Morgan is drying hair in a large beige towel when the phone rings again.
Alan calls and says there has been a small change of plans and they must go up today, storm or no.
Morgan believes the sudden change is a setup, because someone wanted Morgan out of town.
Morgan concludes the setup confirms being on the trail of Sarah.
Morgan plans to call New York and check the local Ninos del Mundo that Barry Morton wanted Morgan to see.
Morgan tests Alan by pointing out that Alan had earlier declared there was no way they would go today.
Alan claims something heavy has come up for tomorrow, so it must be now or forget it for at least a week.
Morgan asks to first see a place in town also called Ninos del Mundo.
Alan says to get the address and maybe they can cruise by if there is time.
Morgan asks Alan for the real story, and Alan insists everything has changed.
Morgan wants to phone Steve so Steve knows where Morgan is.
Alan forbids the phone call, saying there is no time and it can be done after they get back.
Alan orders Morgan to be out front in exactly nineteen minutes and says this is not a dry run.
